_doc: Story-lab scenarios: situations a map's story needs, on one template map (Brackenford). Each has the map context the lines may use (names and their kinds, reward items and a gold budget), the parts a variant writes, the parts the blind packet shows, and Westwood units to set beside ours: [part, csf key or [keys joined as pages]]. Read by tests/storylab.py. Variant 1 takes the situation as written; variants 2-10 each change its specifics (who, which beast, item or place, why) within Brackenford's world, declaring every new person, place or thing they name.

world.summary: Brackenford, a river town of millers and ferrymen on the Bracken, at the edge of the Ashwood. Red Corwin's bandits have taken the old watchtower on Crow Hill, north of town, and rob the north road; Reeve Halvard has shut the north gate until Corwin is dealt with. Wolves have come down out of the Ashwood. Urchins have dug into the old barrow east of the ford. The player is a traveller of unknown class (Warrior, Wizard or Conjurer): never name the class.

scenarios.title: A town guard's barks
scenarios.situation: A guard at a gate or post of the town. Three lines: the first time the player speaks to him, when spoken to again, and later, when something has changed (the quest done, the gate open, the town under attack). In Brackenford: Garrick at the north gate, shut by Reeve Halvard because Red Corwin's bandits rob the north road.

scenarios.title: A reward for a trouble removed
scenarios.situation: Someone in town offers the player a reward to get rid of a trouble: beasts, a nest, a gang, an outlaw with a price on his head. Write the offer, the reminder while it is not done, the thanks and reward, and the journal entry. In Brackenford: Ulric, an old shepherd at the edge of the Ashwood, has lost sheep to the wolves.

scenarios.title: A lost thing fetched, start to end
scenarios.situation: Someone in town has lost a thing to thieves or monsters (useful or magic, as Westwood's are: spectacles, boots, a staff, a scepter, a cloak, an amulet) and asks the player, with a yes/no question, to bring it back. Write the offer, the answer if the player says no, the reminder, the thanks and reward, what the giver says afterwards, the journal entry and the journal entry when it is done. In Brackenford: Wenna, the miller's widow; the Urchins of the old barrow east of the ford took something from the mill.

scenarios.title: Townsfolk
scenarios.situation: Three townsfolk each say one line to the player when spoken to. What townsfolk say in Westwood's towns: a brush-off, gossip, a worry about the times, a tip, a pointer to a place, now and then a word about a quest of the map. In Brackenford the troubles are the wolves of the Ashwood, the Urchins of the old barrow and Red Corwin's bandits on Crow Hill.

scenarios.title: Shopkeepers' greetings
scenarios.situation: Three shopkeepers of the town greet the player: the inn or tavern, the arms and armour shop, the magic shop (potions, scrolls, spell books). In Brackenford: Ossian of the Drowned Lantern inn, Dunstan the smith, Mabry.

scenarios.title: Two asks in one town
scenarios.situation: Two asks the player hears in one town, one from someone respectable, one from someone odd or shady (a deal, a bargain, a jailbreak, a sale), and how each ends. Westwood's are odd or comic deals, not moral forks. In Brackenford: Reeve Halvard wants the tithe chest Red Corwin's bandits stole; Sly Wat, a turncoat of Corwin's, drinks in the Drowned Lantern.

scenarios.title: A rescue
scenarios.situation: Someone in town begs the player to rescue a person (or a pet) held or trapped somewhere. Write the plea, the reminder, what the captive says when found, what the captive says while following the player out, the thanks and reward when the captive is home, and the journal entry. In Brackenford: Brother Anselm's novice Pip went into the old barrow after the Urchins and has not come back.

scenarios.title: The main quest's opening
scenarios.situation: The map's main quest begins: the player arrives, a townsman points him to the one who opens the quest, and that person (a mayor, a captain, a wizard, an old friend of the player's patron) sends him after the chapter's great trouble. Write the townsman's pointer, the opening, the reminder and the journal entry. In Brackenford: Reeve Halvard in the Moot Hall; Red Corwin's bandits hold the old watchtower on Crow Hill and the way north is shut.

scenarios.title: A whole town (one voice across a map)
scenarios.situation: The whole town, by one writer: a quest giver's offer, thanks and journal entry, a guard, a shopkeeper and two townsfolk. The packet sets a cross-section of one of our towns beside a cross-section of one of Westwood's (Ix, Dün Mir, Brin, Galava).
